current_law_statement: Researched from the current published ORS ch. 192 edition supplied as source doc OR_ors192_2026-08-20.txt (oregonlegislature.gov; § 192.324 history ends 2025 c.30 §1, so the 2025 session amendment is already in the base text). MUST-DO 2026 check completed: 2026 Or. Laws ch. 93 (SB 1570, approved 2026-03-31, eff. 2026-06-05) was opened in full — it is a health-care-facility privacy act adding a section to ORS 192.553–192.581 and does NOT amend ORS 192.324 or 192.329; the fee/payment sections are current as printed. Oregon has no administrative rule or uniform statewide fee schedule binding municipal public-records fees: the operative regime for cities is the ORS 192.324(4)(a) actual-cost soft standard plus the fixed $25 estimate-notice gate (192.324(4)(c)) and the 60-day nonpayment close (192.329(3)(b)). Per-page rates seen in the wild (e.g., 25¢/page, $25/hr clerical) are agency-specific policies adopted under the standard, not statewide law. The AG's Public Records and Meetings Manual (guidance layer) was not opened this pass; it cannot supply binding municipal figures and is flagged under gaps.

resolutions.source_language: The public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse the public body for the public body's actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media, to meet the request.
resolutions.notes: No statewide per-page B&W rate for any Oregon public body. The standard is 'fees reasonably calculated to reimburse ... actual cost'; the city supplies the operative rate. ORS 192.311(4) 'public body' expressly includes every city governing body, so the standard binds municipalities. Exception: records filed with the Secretary of State or a county clerk have their own fee regimes (192.324(4)(d), see OR-9003) — not municipal records.

resolutions.notes: No color-specific provision anywhere in ORS 192.311–192.478; color copying is simply one actual-cost component under the same 192.324(4)(a) standard. City sets the operative rate.

resolutions.notes: No oversized/nonstandard-format provision in ORS 192.311–192.478; governed by the general actual-cost standard. City sets the operative rate.

resolutions.notes: Specialty reproduction is expressly inside the standard: 'including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media, to meet the request.' No fixed specialty rates. City sets operative rates within actual cost.

resolutions.manual_verification: AG Public Records and Meetings Manual (guidance) not opened this pass; cannot create binding tiers but could note practice.
resolutions.notes: Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 text opened (fee sections 192.324, 192.329; petition/review 192.407–192.431; advocate 192.461–192.478); no graduated per-page band or volume-tier provision exists; no Oregon administrative rule binds municipal records fees. A city may structure tiers itself so long as the result stays within the 192.324(4)(a) actual-cost standard and it publishes the manner of calculation under 192.324(7)(b) (OR-9004).

resolutions.manual_verification: AG Manual not opened; some Oregon agencies self-adopt free-page allowances as policy, not law.
resolutions.notes: Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no free-page allowance anywhere in the chapter; no administrative rule binds municipal fees. Cities may adopt a free allowance voluntarily (charging is permissive, never mandatory) or waive under 192.324(5) (OR-0023).

resolutions.source_language: The public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse the public body for the public body's actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media, to meet the request.
resolutions.notes: No statutory $/hr search rate; staff search/retrieval time is an actual-cost component under 192.324(4)(a). Rates seen at state agencies (e.g., $25/hr clerical) are agency policy under the standard, not statewide law and not binding on cities. City sets the operative rate.

resolutions.source_language: The public body may include in a fee established under paragraph (a) of this subsection the cost of time spent by an attorney for the public body in reviewing the public records, redacting material from the public records or segregating the public records into exempt and nonexempt records. The public body may not include in a fee established under paragraph (a) of this subsection the cost of time spent by an attorney for the public body in determining the application of the provisions of ORS 192.311 to 192.478.
resolutions.notes: No $/hr rate. Review/redaction time — including attorney review/redaction/segregation time — is chargeable at actual cost; attorney time spent determining whether the exemptions APPLY is expressly NOT chargeable (192.324(4)(b), OR-0021). City sets the operative rate within actual cost.

resolutions.source_language: The public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse the public body for the public body's actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media, to meet the request.
resolutions.notes: Programming/data extraction sits squarely in 'summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media'. No fixed rate; city sets the operative $/hr within actual cost.

resolutions.value: always (no page/hour threshold); attorney exemption-analysis time never chargeable
resolutions.source_language: The public body may not include in a fee established under paragraph (a) of this subsection the cost of time spent by an attorney for the public body in determining the application of the provisions of ORS 192.311 to 192.478.
resolutions.notes: Shape: labor is chargeable from the first minute (no free-hours or page threshold gates it), bounded only by the actual-cost standard; the sole categorical carve-out is attorney time analyzing whether exemptions apply (Prohibition, OR-0021). Charging is permissive — a city may choose not to charge. The >$25 estimate gate (OR-0022) conditions COLLECTING a larger fee, not whether labor is billable.

resolutions.source_language: The public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse the public body for the public body's actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media, to meet the request.
resolutions.manual_verification: Whether benefits/overhead loading is 'actual cost' for an Oregon city is a scope judgment on the standard — no statute or rule speaks to a percentage; AG Manual guidance not opened.
resolutions.notes: No express overhead/fringe surcharge provision anywhere in ORS 192.311–192.478 (contrast Michigan's 50% fringe cap). Any loading a city applies must fit within 'reasonably calculated to reimburse ... actual cost'; no statutory percentage exists.

resolutions.manual_verification: AG Manual not opened; increments (e.g., quarter-hour) appear only in agency-specific policies.
resolutions.notes: Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no billing-increment or rounding provision; no administrative rule binds municipal fees. City sets its own increment within the actual-cost standard and publishes the manner of calculation (192.324(7)(b), OR-9004).

Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no free-labor-hours allowance (contrast WA/TN first-hour-free patterns); no administrative rule binds municipal fees. Labor is chargeable from the first minute (see labor.billableWhen); a city may self-adopt a free allowance.
Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no TX § 552.275-style per-requestor periodic free-time ledger or requestor-level cap exists in Oregon law.

resolutions.unit: USD (estimated fee; written notice + requester confirmation required to exceed)
resolutions.source_language: The public body may not establish a fee greater than $25 under this section unless the public body first provides the requester with a written notification of the estimated amount of the fee and the requester confirms that the requester wants the public body to proceed with making the public record available.
resolutions.notes: Fixed statutory trigger — a city cannot raise it. Above $25 the body must send a written fee estimate AND obtain the requester's confirmation before proceeding. Confirmed unchanged by 2025 c.30 §1 (in base text) and untouched by 2026 c.93. Binds all public bodies including cities (ORS 192.311(4)).

resolutions.unit: calendar days from the date the public body informed the requester of the fee (or of the fee-waiver denial); on lapse without payment the request is closed
resolutions.source_language: If the requester fails to pay the fee within 60 days of the date on which the public body informed the requester of the fee, or fails to pay the fee within 60 days of the date on which the public body informed the requester of the denial of the fee waiver, the public body shall close the request.
resolutions.notes: Oregon frames the window as pay-within-60-days rather than confirm-the-estimate-within-N-days: the >$25 estimate must be confirmed (192.324(4)(c)) with no stated confirmation deadline, but the 60-day payment clock from fee notification is the operative response window — nonresponse/nonpayment for 60 days mandatorily closes the request. Prior slice's '$25' value on this item belonged to the threshold item, not this one.

Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no revised-estimate or variance-percentage provision. Related but distinct: a requester who believes a written fee estimate exceeds actual cost may seek Public Records Advocate facilitated dispute resolution (192.464(2)(c)) — mandatory-on-request only against STATE AGENCIES; for a city it requires agreement of both the city and the requester plus the advocate's consent (192.464(1)(b), (6)). Prior slice's '$25' value belonged to the threshold item.

Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no estimate expiry/validity period. The functional outer bound is the 60-day nonpayment close (192.329(3)(b)): an unconfirmed/unpaid fee ends the request at 60 days rather than the estimate expiring.

resolutions.value: no dollar threshold — full prepayment enforceable at any fee amount via suspension of the response obligation
resolutions.source_language: If a public body has informed a requester of a fee permitted under ORS 192.324 (4), the obligation of the public body to complete its response to the request is suspended until the requester has paid the fee, the fee has been waived by the public body pursuant to ORS 192.324 (5) or the fee otherwise has been ordered waived.
resolutions.notes: Oregon has no deposit-specific scheme (no threshold, no partial-deposit machinery). Instead, once ANY permitted fee is noticed, the body's duty to complete its response is suspended until payment/waiver — i.e., prepayment in full is enforceable at any amount, subject to the >$25 estimate+confirmation gate (OR-0022) before a fee above $25 may be established.

Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no deposit-cap percentage (no deposit scheme at all; see rules.deposit.threshold). The statute contemplates payment of the noticed fee, not a partial deposit.

resolutions.value: pay-before-completion: response obligation suspended until noticed fee is paid, waived, or ordered waived
resolutions.source_language: If a public body has informed a requester of a fee permitted under ORS 192.324 (4), the obligation of the public body to complete its response to the request is suspended until the requester has paid the fee, the fee has been waived by the public body pursuant to ORS 192.324 (5) or the fee otherwise has been ordered waived.
resolutions.notes: Production may lawfully be conditioned on payment: the completion duty is statutorily suspended while a noticed fee is unpaid. Exit ramps: payment, the body's own 192.324(5) waiver, or a waiver ordered on review (192.324(6), 192.407(3)(c) — OR-9001/OR-9002).

resolutions.unit: calendar days from fee notification (or fee-waiver denial); the public body SHALL close the request on lapse
resolutions.source_language: If the requester fails to pay the fee within 60 days of the date on which the public body informed the requester of the fee, or fails to pay the fee within 60 days of the date on which the public body informed the requester of the denial of the fee waiver, the public body shall close the request.
resolutions.notes: Mandatory close ('shall'), fixed 60-day count, two alternative start events (fee notice; waiver denial). No prior-debt-prepayment provision exists in ORS 192. Untouched by 2026 c.93.

resolutions.value: clock effect: completion obligation tolled while noticed fee unpaid; lapse action: mandatory close at 60 days; no grace period stated
resolutions.source_language: If a public body has informed a requester of a fee permitted under ORS 192.324 (4), the obligation of the public body to complete its response to the request is suspended until the requester has paid the fee, the fee has been waived by the public body pursuant to ORS 192.324 (5) or the fee otherwise has been ordered waived.
resolutions.notes: Applies to the noticed FEE (Oregon has no deposit scheme): (3)(a) tolls the completion duty from fee notification until payment/waiver; (3)(b) is the terminal event — mandatory close at 60 days. The engine's deposit-clock knobs map to fee-clock: effect=tolls, grace=none, lapse=close.

resolutions.manual_verification: Whether a final fee exceeding a confirmed estimate requires fresh 192.324(4)(c) notice is unaddressed in statute; AG Manual/AG opinions not swept.
resolutions.notes: Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no overrun/re-issue provision (no revised-estimate duty, no collection block, no window restart). The only estimate machinery is the >$25 notice+confirmation gate (OR-0022); the statute does not say what happens when actual cost exceeds the confirmed estimate. Do not infer a re-notice duty.

resolutions.source_language: The public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse the public body for the public body's actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media, to meet the request.
resolutions.notes: Request-level cap is the soft standard itself: fees must be 'reasonably calculated to reimburse ... actual cost' — no dollar maximum. Enforcement teeth: a requester who believes an estimate exceeds actual cost can invoke 192.464(2)(c) FDR (agencies; cities only by mutual agreement) or petition on waiver/reduction grounds.

Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no de-minimis no-charge floor. Distinct: the discretionary public-interest waiver (192.324(5), OR-0023) lets a custodian furnish copies free, but that is a public-interest determination, not a below-$X rule. A city may self-adopt a de-minimis floor (charging is permissive).

Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no minimum-fee provision. Any city minimum must still be 'reasonably calculated to reimburse ... actual cost' (192.324(4)(a)); a flat minimum untethered from cost would strain the standard.

resolutions.source_language: The public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse the public body for the public body's actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media, to meet the request.
resolutions.notes: Physical media (CD/DVD/USB) is an actual-cost component — the standard expressly reaches tailoring 'in organization or media'. Note 192.324(3): electronic records must be provided in the requested form if available (a duty, no separate fee rule). City sets media charges at actual cost.

resolutions.source_language: The public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse the public body for the public body's actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media, to meet the request.
resolutions.manual_verification: Postage/handling is not enumerated in 192.324(4)(a); treating mailing as 'actual cost of making public records available' is the settled reading (AG guidance) but is a scope judgment on the statute.
resolutions.notes: No delivery-specific statute. Mailing/postage is conventionally recovered as actual cost under the general standard; no rate exists. City sets delivery charges at actual cost; email delivery has no statutory charge basis beyond staff time actually incurred.

resolutions.manual_verification: Record-specific certification fee statutes (vital records, court records) exist outside ch. 192 and were not inventoried; none is general municipal authority.
resolutions.notes: Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no certified-copy fee for municipal records; a city certification charge falls back to the 192.324(4)(a) actual-cost standard. Contrast the carved-out regimes (OR-9003): records filed with a COUNTY CLERK carry fixed fees under ORS 205.320 (certification $3.75 per official certificate; copies 25 cents/page + up to $3.75 locating) — county authority, not municipal.

resolutions.source_language: The public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse the public body for the public body's actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media, to meet the request.
resolutions.notes: 'Writing' includes 'sounds' and 'electronic recordings' (ORS 192.311(7)), so audio/video duplication (including redaction labor, e.g. body-cam blurring) is priced under the same actual-cost standard. No per-recording, per-minute, or free-minutes figures exist. City sets operative rates.

Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no commercial-purpose fee schedule, surcharge, or purpose-statement requirement in the general public-records fee law. (Record-specific commercial-use restrictions exist elsewhere in Oregon law, e.g. DMV records, but create no municipal records-fee differential.) The public-interest waiver (192.324(5)) lets purpose cut fees DOWN, never up.

resolutions.value: discretionary public-interest waiver/reduction; no purpose statement required; denial reviewable by petition to AG/DA/court; reviewing body may also order waiver for untimely response
resolutions.source_language: The custodian of a public record may furnish copies without charge or at a substantially reduced fee if the custodian determines that the waiver or reduction of fees is in the public interest because making the record available primarily benefits the general public.
resolutions.notes: Shape: (1) grounds = public interest / primarily benefits the general public (192.324(5), OR-0023) — DISCRETIONARY ('may'), never mandatory; (2) no statutory purpose-statement or written-denial-form requirement; (3) appeal = petition to AG or DA 'in the same manner as' a records-denial petition, with the same AG/DA/court authority (192.324(6), OR-9001); (4) a reviewing body may independently ORDER a waiver/reduction where the body responded with undue delay (192.407(3)(c), OR-9002). Waiver denial also starts a 60-day payment clock (192.329(3)(b)).

resolutions.value: no automatic forfeiture; AG/DA/court MAY order a fee waiver or reduction on petition if the body responded with undue delay or failed to respond as prescribed
resolutions.source_language: If the Attorney General, the district attorney or a court grants a petition filed under this section, the order granting the petition: ... (c) May order a fee waiver or a fee reduction if a public body has responded to the request with undue delay or has failed to respond to the request in the time and manner prescribed in ORS 192.329. Nothing in this subsection prohibits a reviewing body from finding an unreasonable denial of a fee waiver or a fee reduction on other grounds.
resolutions.notes: Oregon has a late-response fee consequence, but it is remedial and discretionary, not self-executing: forfeiture happens only if a requester petitions under 192.407 and the AG/DA/court orders the waiver (the same order may also carry a $200 penalty for undue delay, 192.407(3)(b) — penalty amount out of engine scope). Engine flag fee_forfeiture_on_late_response = not automatic; surfaces as a review-outcome state. Prior slice's '60 days' value belonged to the nonpayment item, not this one.

Coverage: full ORS 192.311–192.478 opened — no repeat-request carry-forward, prior-unpaid-balance prepayment, or multi-request aggregation provision (contrast SC's 6-month re-request bar or TX aggregation). Each request stands alone; the only closure-and-return path is the 60-day nonpayment close with no statutory bar on re-requesting.

new_rules.legal_concept: Petition to Attorney General or district attorney on unreasonable denial of fee waiver or reduction
new_rules.atomic_rule: A requester who believes a fee waiver or fee reduction was unreasonably denied may petition the Attorney General or the district attorney in the same manner as a requester petitions when inspection of a public record is denied; the AG, DA and court have the same authority as in a denial-of-inspection petition.
new_rules.trigger: Requester believes there has been an unreasonable denial of a fee waiver or fee reduction under ORS 192.324(5)
new_rules.source_language: A requester who believes that there has been an unreasonable denial of a fee waiver or fee reduction may petition the Attorney General or the district attorney in the same manner as a requester who petitions when inspection of a public record is denied under ORS 192.311 to 192.478. The Attorney General, the district attorney and the court have the same authority in instances when a fee waiver or reduction is denied as when inspection of a public record is denied.
new_rules.notes: The waiver-denial appeal path missing from the existing corpus (OR-0023's notes referenced reviewability but no row carried it). AG petitions route to the AG for state agencies and to the DA for local bodies under the 192.411/192.415 pattern; either way the review right binds cities. A waiver denial also starts the 60-day payment clock (OR-0025).

new_rules.legal_concept: Ordered fee waiver or reduction as remedy for undue delay or failure to respond
new_rules.atomic_rule: If the AG, DA or a court grants a petition under ORS 192.407, the order MAY require a fee waiver or fee reduction where the public body responded to the request with undue delay or failed to respond in the time and manner prescribed in ORS 192.329; a reviewing body may also find an unreasonable waiver denial on other grounds.
new_rules.trigger: Petition under ORS 192.407 granted after public body's undue delay or failure to respond as prescribed by ORS 192.329
new_rules.source_language: If the Attorney General, the district attorney or a court grants a petition filed under this section, the order granting the petition: (a) May require disclosure of nonexempt material responsive to the request within seven days, or within any other period that the Attorney General, district attorney or court concludes is appropriate to comply with ORS 192.329; (b) May require the public body to pay a penalty of $200 to the requester if the Attorney General, district attorney or court determines that the public body responded to the request with undue delay or failed to respond to the request; and (c) May order a fee waiver or a fee reduction if a public body has responded to the request with undue delay or has failed to respond to the request in the time and manner prescribed in ORS 192.329. Nothing in this subsection prohibits a reviewing body from finding an unreasonable denial of a fee waiver or a fee reduction on other grounds.
new_rules.notes: Oregon's fee-forfeiture-on-late-response analogue: discretionary and remedial (requires a petition and an order), never self-executing. The $200 penalty in (3)(b) is a remedy amount (out of engine scope under the V1/V2 Remove list) — retained here only because it rides in the same operative sentence; the operative engine fact is the orderable waiver in (3)(c).

new_rules.legal_concept: Carve-out fee regimes for records filed with the Secretary of State or a county clerk
new_rules.atomic_rule: Notwithstanding the actual-cost fee rules of ORS 192.324(4)(a)-(c), fees for records filed with the Secretary of State under ORS ch. 79A or ORS 81.230–81.263 are those set by Secretary of State rule, and fees for copies of records filed with a county clerk are those established under ORS 205.320.
new_rules.trigger: Requested public records are those filed with the Secretary of State (ORS ch. 79A / 81.230–81.263) or with a county clerk
new_rules.source_language: Notwithstanding paragraphs (a) to (c) of this subsection, when the public records are those filed with: (A) The Secretary of State under ORS chapter 79A or ORS 81.230 to 81.263, the fees for furnishing copies, summaries or compilations of the public records are the fees established by the Secretary of State by rule under ORS chapter 79A or ORS 81.230 to 81.263. (B) A county clerk, the fees for copies of records are the fees established under ORS 205.320.
new_rules.notes: NOT municipal authority — neither branch applies to city-held records; recorded because it bounds the reach of OR-0020/OR-0022. Delegation (B) followed: ORS 205.320 (opened, 2025 c.31 §2 current) fixes county-clerk figures — copies 25 cents/page plus not more than $3.75 for locating a record; official certificate $3.75; recording $5/page. Delegation (A) (SoS UCC-type filings) deliberately not pursued: no municipal item depends on it.

new_rules.legal_concept: Public body must publish written request procedure including fee amounts and manner of calculation
new_rules.atomic_rule: A public body shall make available to the public a written public-records-request procedure that includes the name(s) and address(es) of the individual(s) to whom requests may be sent and the amounts of and manner of calculating the fees the body charges for responding to requests.
new_rules.trigger: None stated (standing duty of every public body)
new_rules.source_language: A public body shall make available to the public a written procedure for making public records requests that includes: (a) The name of one or more individuals within the public body to whom public records requests may be sent, with addresses; and (b) The amounts of and the manner of calculating fees that the public body charges for responding to requests for public records.
new_rules.notes: The statutory hook that makes every fee value in Oregon a CITY-published figure: the state supplies the standard and the $25/60-day machinery, the city must publish its own amounts and calculation method. Also the anchor for the 5-business-day acknowledgment duty (192.324(2) keys on the individual identified in this procedure). Platform surface: published fee-schedule page.

applicability_notes: ORS 192.311(4) defines 'public body' to include 'every county and city governing body, school district, special district, municipal corporation, and any board, department, commission, council, or agency thereof' — every ch. 192 fee/payment rule in this pass (actual-cost standard, $25 estimate gate, fee-suspension toll, 60-day close, waiver machinery) binds municipalities directly; applies_to = all_public_bodies throughout.

Oregon has NO statewide uniform fee schedule and NO administrative rule binding municipal records fees. Per-page and per-hour figures published by state agencies (e.g., 25 cents/page, $25/hr clerical on agency policy pages) are agency-specific policies adopted UNDER the 192.324(4)(a) standard — guidance-layer only for a city, never a municipal ceiling or default.

The two carved-out fixed-fee regimes (192.324(4)(d): Secretary of State filings by SoS rule; county-clerk records under ORS 205.320) are record-specific and never apply to city-held records (OR-9003).

Public Records Advocate facilitated dispute resolution over fee estimates/waiver denials (192.464) is mandatory-on-request only against STATE AGENCIES; for a city it requires the agreement of both parties plus the advocate's consent, and the good-faith sanctions of 192.464(4)-(5) do not apply (192.464(6)).

Every operative fee VALUE in Oregon is city-set: 192.324(7)(b) obliges each public body to publish 'the amounts of and the manner of calculating fees' (OR-9004) — the state contributes the standard, the $25 notice gate, and the payment clock.
material_negatives: No numeric fee figure of any kind binds Oregon municipalities except the $25 estimate-notice trigger and the 60-day nonpayment/no-response-to-waiver-denial close — every rate, tier, allowance, deposit, minimum, and media/delivery/certification charge is city-set under the actual-cost standard.
No deposit scheme exists (no threshold, no percentage cap, no partial-deposit machinery); the fee-suspension mechanism of 192.329(3)(a) does the prepayment work at any amount.
No commercial-purpose fee differential, purpose-statement requirement, or requester-class pricing in the general public-records law.
No free-page, free-labor-hour, or per-requestor periodic free-time allowance.
No estimate-revision, estimate-validity, or overrun re-notice provision.
No automatic fee forfeiture for late response — only a discretionary, petition-triggered ordered waiver (192.407(3)(c)).

Absence caveat: these negatives cover ORS 192.311–192.478 (full chapter text opened) plus a targeted official-source sweep; the AG Public Records and Meetings Manual and formal AG opinions were not exhaustively swept (they cannot create binding municipal figures, but could document settled interpretations).
gaps_manual_verification: AG Public Records and Meetings Manual (Oregon DOJ) not opened this pass — guidance layer; would firm up the medium-confidence scope judgments on delivery/postage-as-actual-cost, overhead loading, and billing increments, and could document settled interpretation of overrun re-notice under the $25 gate.
Whether a final fee exceeding a confirmed >$25 estimate requires a fresh 192.324(4)(c) notice is statutorily unaddressed (payment.reissue) — AG opinion sweep would help.
Record-specific certification-fee statutes outside ch. 192 (vital records, court records, police reports) were not inventoried; none is general municipal records authority.

2026 c.93 was verified in full text; the 2026 A&R Tables themselves were not separately opened (the chapter header named ch. 93 as the only 2026 act touching ch. 192, and ch. 93 is confirmed non-fee).
